 JUDGMENT
This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 13.10.2023 at about 11.00 p.m, the petitioner and his friends were coming by bikes from their native place and had parked their bikes in MRPL Petrol Bunk and went to Menaka Daba, near Avverahalli Gate, NH- 75 Mandya for dinner and there was no food in that (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 daba, hence they were return in their bikes to go for their native, while crossing NH-75 Road on the left side, on that moment suddenly a rider of Motor Cycle Honda Bike/SP 125 BS VI bearing No.KA-13-EY-2174 came from Bengaluru side towards Mangaluru side, in rash and negligent manner, with high speed and dashed against the petitioner and his friend Mohan Kumar.T.L.
Due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to A.C. Giri hospital, Bellur Cross and same day he was discharged and again he was treated as inpatient from 16.10.2023 to 18.10.2023.
After the accident the petitioner is taking treatment and psychotherapy on regular basis by incurring additional expenditure which has reached few lakhs as on today.

The petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/-
towards hospitalization, transportation and for medicines and nourishment.

Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 44 years and was working as Chef in Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he has undergone tremendous pain both physically and mentally and it has made his idle without any work and his life has become miserable.

The accident is (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 occurred due to rash and negligent riding of offending Motor Cycle involved in the accident and in this regard the Bindiganavile Police have registered a case against driver of the said offending Motor Cycle.

Hence,
the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the said offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsels and filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued the policy to the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-13-EY-2174 and liability to indemnify the respondent No.2 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and Pradeep Kumar T H vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146218268/
2 contended that the owner/rider of the Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-13-EY-2174 was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and further was not qualified for holding or obtaining such driving licence

The compensation claimed is exorbitant.

Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

The respondent No.2 in his written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and the compensation claimed is highly excessive and stated that he is the owner of the offending Motor Cycle and the rider of the offending Motor Cycle was having valid driving licence to ride the motor bike and the said Motor Cycle was duly insured with respondent No.1 and hence, pray to dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.

06. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 13.10.2023 at about 11.00 p.m, on NH-75 Bengaluru-Mangaluru Road, Avverahalli Gate, near Avverahalli Village, Bindiganavile, Nagamangala, due to rash and (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 negligent riding of rider of Honda Bike bearing registration No.KA-13-EY-2174 as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?

07. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined MRO as PW.2 and through them got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 and closed the petitioner side evidence.
The respondent No.1 got examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and through him got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.

08. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits his side arguments may be taken as heard, hence,
petitioner side arguments is taken as heard and the learned counsel for the respondents have argued on main matter and perused the records.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, he him examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.1 counsel he denied to the suggestion that there are three persons are riding the Motor Cycle and skid and fall and sustained injuries and since the rider of the Motor Cycle had no driving licence and Motor Cycle had no RC and insurance, in order to get compensation they have falsely implicated the offending Motor Cycle in the accident and he admits that after discharge from the Adichunchanagiri hospital he has not taken further treatment at any hospital and he has not produced any document to show that he is working as a Cook.
11.
PW.2 is Medical Record Officer at A.C. Giri hospital, B.G.Nagar and he has produced copy of MLC, Police intimation, OPD slip, Inpatient record and X-ray as per Ex.P.14 to 18.
During the cross examination by (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 respondent No.1 counsel he states that he does not know the contents of documents produced by him.
12. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 on his behalf.
Ex.P.1 is the Copy of FIR filed by the Bindiganavile Police against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.2 is copy of the Complaint.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar along with Sketch.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Statement of petitioner.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report which shows involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Wound Certificate, which shows that the petitioner has sustained three injuries in the road traffic accident, out of which injury No.3 is grievous in nature.

Ex.P.7 is copy of Charge sheet, which discloses that the Investigation Officer after through investigation has submitted the Charge sheet against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle for rash and negligent riding, causing accident and grievous injuries to the petitioner and it also appears that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has invoked provisions of Sec.181(3) of IMV Act against rider of the offending Motor Cycle for riding the Motor Cycle without driving licence.

Ex.P.8 is Discharge summary of Adichunchanagiri hospital, B.G. Nagara, which shows (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient on 16.10.2023 and discharged on 18.10.2023 for 3 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.14 is copy of MLC.
Ex.P.15 is copy of Police intimation.
Ex.P.16 is OPD slip.
Ex.P.17 is Inpatient record and Ex.P.18 is X-ray.

13. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has clearly established and proved that he had sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 13.10.2023 at about 11.00 p.m, on NH-75 Road, Avverahalli Gate, Avverahalli Village,
Bindiganavile Hobli, Mandya, due to rash and negligent act of riding of rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-13-EY-2174, by its rider as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road traffic accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 44 years and was working as Chef in Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospitalization, (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 transportation and for medicines and nourishment.
Due to accidental injuries, he has undergone tremendous pain both physically and mentally and it has made his idle without any work and his life has become miserable.
15. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, she has produced Ex.P.11 copy of Aadhaar card and Ex.P.12 PAN card.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other evidence, the said documents can be taken into consideration, according to which, date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 29.09.1979.
The alleged accident occurred on 13.10.2023 and hence, it appears that at the time of accident the age of petitioner is 44 years.
Accordingly, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 44 years as on the date of accident.

16. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, absolutely there is no evidence or materials in this regard and according to Ex.P.9 Medical bills, he has incurrred medical expenses of Rs.1,026/- only.
According to Ex.P.8 Discharge (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 summary the petitioner took treatment as inpatient only for 3 days.

It is pertinent to note that petitioner in this case has not examined the doctor who treated him and has not produced any disability certificate to establish that he has sustained any physical or functional disability due to accidental injuries and there is no evidence on record to show that he sustained loss of future income or loss of income during laid up period and even there is no evidence on record to show that he needs another surgery or any future medical expenses.

Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/-.
17.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

18. Regarding liability:- The respondent No.1 Insurance Company to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove its defence, its Legal Manager is examined as RW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the written statement averments therein and got marked copy of Policy at Ex.R.2.

During the course of cross-examination by the (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 petitioner counsel he admits that they have issued insurance policy to the offending Motor Cycle and same is valid as on the date of accident.

19. In this case the respondent No.1 Insurance Company has taken contention that though it has issued insurance policy in favour of the respondent No.2, but it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy with respect to valid driving licence and in this case the rider of the Motor Cycle had no Pradeep Kumar T H vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146218268/
5 driving licence at all and hence, respondent No.1 is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P.7 Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle who rode the Motor Cycle without driving licence.
As per Ex.R.2 copy of Policy, the said policy is valid as on the date of accident.

But there is a condition that 3rd party risk covers only when the person driving holds an effective driving licence at the time of accident, and he is not disqualified from holding or obtaining such a licence.
Therefore, it is clear cut case of violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

Either the petitioner or the respondent No.2 owner of the offending Motor Cycle or rider of the offending Motor Cycle have not produced any copy of driving licence or driving licence extract to show that as on the date of accident the rider of the (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 offending Motor Cycle had a valid driving licence and thereby, the owner is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and it is Insurance Company to pay compensation to the petitioner.
But no such evidence are placed before the tribunal.
Therefore, it appears that the rider of the offending Motor Cycle had rode the Motor Cycle without driving licence and caused accident.

Therefore, since there is a clear cut case of fundamental violation of terms and conditions of the policy, the owner is liable to pay compensation and Insurance Company absolved from the payment of compensation.
In this regard the following citations are relevant.
L.J 249 in a case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Annemma and others,

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Annemma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 Sec.149(1) insurer is under no liability to indemnify the insurer's risk.
This is an insurer's appeal Held: It is a clear case of breach of the terms of the contract with the insurer -
The insurer pleaded its defence and produced the copy of notice issued to the owner calling upon him to produce his license.

The owner maintaining silence without responding to the notice of the insurer by itself is (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 sufficient proof of defence though without any effort to prove the negative i.e., absence of valid driving licenseValid defence statutorily available under Section 149(1) of the Act having raised and established the insurer is under no liability to indemnify the insurer's risk to the third party.

At the same time, there can not be any order against the Insurance Company to satisfy the third party claim and then recover from the owner in the light of the ruling of the Division Bench of this Court".

(Para 16) In MFA No.100226/2016 (MV) and MFA No.100730/2016 in between Smt.Padma and others V/s Ramanjali Naidu and others, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "A person who had no driving license or not renewed for 30 days, the driver neither had effective driving license nor said licence is duly licenced.

insured/owner is liable to pay compensation to the claimant and absolved Insurance Company from liability" and also relied upon decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in Civil Appeal No.7220 and 7221 of 2011 in a case of Beliram V/s. Rajinder Kumar and another, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court held that, (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.7639/2023 "(E) Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 Sec.14, 15 and 149(2)(a)(ii) - Driving licence expired - Driving licence having expired led to the natural finding that there was no valid driving license on the date of the accident.

Since no evidence had been led in this behalf, a presumption was drawn that there was willful and conscious breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy"

Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The claim petition against respondent No.1 Insurance Company is hereby dismissed on without costs.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
